newsitem.title: USA: NAIC view on new preferred stock may boost demand.
newsitem.headline: NAIC view on new preferred stock may boost demand.

text.p: An expected recommendation by the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC) that would require insurance companies treat a new type of preferred stock as debt for risk-based capital purposes is likely to fuel insurance company demand for the new securities, according to corporate bond market analysts.

Analysts said stronger demand for the securities is likely to increase selling pressure on outstanding 10- to 30-year bank bonds, which have already experienced a widening of spreads of up to 15 basis points since the new securities have been issued.
Banks have already issued approximately $4.0 billion of the new tax-advantaged preferred securities and an additional $10 billion are expected to be issued over the next several months.
The securities resemble bonds as they have fixed-maturites, non-call provisions and are senior to preferred stock in the credit heirarchy.

The Invested Asset Working Group of the NAIC will meet at 1300 EST/1800 GMT on Tuesday to consider the issue. Its decision will guide the NAIC's Securities Valuation Office, which will make the final decision.
According to NAIC rules, preferred stock require a two percent additional capital charge compared to bonds, making it more economical for insurance companies to hold bonds.
Based on previous correspondences between the NAIC and investment banks, analysts expect the insurance regulator to treat the preferred stock as debt.
A NAIC spokeswoman declined to comment on any potential decision.
A NAIC recommendation to treat the securities as debt may also lead Lehman Brothers Inc to include the new securities in its fixed-income indexes, analysts said.
That would significantly increase demand for the preferred stock from pension fund managers and other money managers who use the indexes to measure porfolio performance, analysts said.
A Lehman spokesman confirmed that the firm was considering adding the securities to its indexes, but could not provide further details.
Salomon Brothers has already included the new securities in its Salomon Brothers Broad Investment-Grade Bond Index.

The NAIC decision coupled with continued new supply of preferred paper, "could conceivably widen spreads by a couple of basis points to a nickel (or five basis points) across most intermediate and longer-term bank debt securities this week," said Joseph Labriola, director of corporate bond research at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell
